objective: Verify HMR does not apply an intermediate source version when a file changes between watcher emission and source preparation
method: A live quench-node --hmr process loaded a self-accepted .mjs entry. The file was atomically replaced with generation 2 containing a 4 MB comment, then atomically replaced with generation 3 75 ms later while preparation of the changed source was intentionally made more expensive. The process output was observed for 8 seconds after the second edit.
scope: One local macOS stress run. It verifies the user-visible outcome for closely spaced atomic edits; there is no instrumentation proving the precise instruction at which the second edit overlapped preparation.

scenarios.description: Two valid atomic replacements separated by 75 ms while a 4 MB comment lengthened preparation.

An invalid intermediate ESM source (4 MB comment followed by `const = ;`) was atomically replaced by a valid self-accepted generation 75 ms later. Initial generation 0 and final generation 3 were observed.

result: Both rapid-edit runs left the process alive and applied only the final valid generation; the invalid intermediate source emitted no HMR diagnostic.
